summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics) with the harness assurance_generated_test.go; scratch removed. This turn requests a successor experiment for the removed-leader finding that addresses its strongest recorded objection - that the earlier progress windows used a fixed round-robin tick order. The basis change is stated in the submission: the window now rotates the node tick order each round and reverses the delivery order of the produced messages on alternating rounds, with every node still ticked once per round and every message still delivered through the real Step path, so it is a scheduling variation rather than a fault injection; the same two comparisons are re-measured on that basis, with the removal and the StepDownOnRemoval control unchanged. Construction-time local runs show, for the record and not as formal evidence, the same contrast the experiment is built to capture: over 120 varied-schedule rounds the cluster that removed its leader without step-down never elected an eligible leader (states still leader-plus-followers, last index and committed index unchanged at 2, nothing undelivered, eligible voters' election timers still being reset), while the step-down control elected node 3 inside the same window. That confines any dependence of the stall on the earlier ordering, and the prefix, scope and assumptions spell out exactly what varies and what does not; the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained receipt.
